scope: Gen. Bus. Law § 1420 as it decides who is bound and what is reportable (foundation model, frontier model, frontier developer, large frontier developer, catastrophic risk, the four kinds of critical safety incident) and § 1423; § 1422(1), (3)(a)-(c), (6), (8)-(10) (the 72-hour report to the office within the Department of Financial Services, counted in minutes on the UTC scale from the earlier of determination and reasonable belief; the 24-hour disclosure; amended reports; the report's four items; the FOIL exemption; the federal deemed-compliance route); §§ 1425, 1426 as inputs; § 1427(1), (2) (large frontier developers only; up to $1,000,000 first and $3,000,000 per subsequent violation; Attorney General only); § 1428(5) (amount only); L. 2026, ch. 96 §§ 3, 5 (effective 2027-01-01). Inert, out of scope or deferred, each with a row in NOTES.md: § 1421, § 1422(2), (4), (5), (7), § 1424, § 1427(3), § 1428(1)-(4), (6), § 1429, ch. 96 §§ 1, 4.

forks.F1: Every frontier developer must report (§ 1422(3)(a)); only a large one is subject to the § 1427 penalty.
forks.F2: Every threshold is strict: more than 10^26 operations, more than $500,000,000, more than 50 people, more than $1,000,000,000.
forks.F3: A frontier model has already used more than 10^26 operations; a frontier developer has trained or begun a foundation model for which it has used or intends to use more than 10^26.
forks.F4: 'Subject to paragraph (b)': both the 72-hour report and the 24-hour disclosure are owed.
forks.F5: A catastrophic risk has 'materialized' when the event it describes, at its stated size, has happened and no exclusion applies.
forks.F6: The four kinds overlap; every kind that fits is listed.
forks.F7: Deployment is not an element of the reporting duty.
forks.F8: Two starting events (determination; facts sufficient for a reasonable belief): the 72 hours run from whichever came first.
forks.F9: No time zone or counting rule is stated: moments carry their UTC offset and are counted on the UTC scale; no weekend or holiday extension; the General Construction Law was not deposited (host blocked) and its content is recalled, not checked.
forks.F10: A report at exactly 72 hours (a disclosure at exactly 24) is within the period.
forks.F11: § 1422(1)'s mechanism contents are read as what the report gives.
forks.F12: The deposited page prints '10§26'; read as 10^26.
forks.F13: The federal route is one input; no designation is known.
forks.F14: A clock that started before 2027-01-01 is not covered; whether the 2025 article was briefly in force (its 90th day, by a plain count 2026-03-19, preceded chapter 96's signing on 2026-03-27) is not decided.
forks.F15: 'the preceding calendar year' is not anchored; revenue is one input.
forks.F16: The 24-hour duty is read literally: not limited to the developer's own frontier models.
forks.F17: The 24-hour recipient is a class ('an authority ... appropriate ... and as required by law'); none is named.
forks.F18: Whether § 1427 reaches a failed 24-hour disclosure is not plain; the answer says so.
forks.F19: How violations are counted is not stated; the developer says whether this is its first.
forks.F20: § 1428(5) speaks of a 'large frontier model', a term § 1420 does not define; only the amount is computed.
forks.F21: § 1422(6) cites § 1421 for internal-use assessment reports that § 1422(2) requires; recorded, not encoded.
forks.F22: A fine-tuner of another developer's base model: whether the base model's training run counts toward its compute (§ 1420(9)(b) 'the developer applies'); not decided, the compute inputs leave it to the developer.
forks.F23: Whose 'determination' starts the 72-hour clock (§ 1422(3)(a) names no actor): read as the developer's own; open.
forks.F24: § 1426(1) 'to the extent' limits the university exception to academic research; the input asks about that research only.
forks.F25: § 1420(14) 'Person' covers only nongovernmental bodies, so a governmental body cannot be a frontier developer; not encoded as an input.
forks.F26: § 1422(7) the office's annual report is transmitted to named officials; the text does not say it is published. Inert.
